text: Joanna Mary Seagar MNZM (born 1955), commonly known as Jo Seagar, is a New Zealand writer, TV personality, and celebrity cook. She resides in the small town of Oxford in North Canterbury with her husband Ross. Seagar initially trained as a nurse and attended Le Cordon Bleu cookery school in London while working at the Royal Free Hospital. Upon returning to New Zealand, she co-founded Harley's Restaurant in Auckland with fellow nurse Helen Brabazon. She later operated "Seagars at Oxford," a cooking school, café, and kitchenware store, for approximately ten years before it closed in 2015. Seagar attributed the closure to the decline in tourism caused by the Canterbury earthquakes. The closure resulted in thousands of dollars remaining unpaid to employees and creditors. She has been the first food writer for North & South, has contributed to New Zealand Woman's Weekly and Cuisine magazine, and regularly writes a column for the Australian Women's Weekly. Seagar serves as a patron and ambassador for Hospice, raising funds for the charity through cooking classes. In the 2015 New Year Honours, she was appointed a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit for services to the community.
